audience: adults with ADHD, or executive function that works like it, who have tried planners and to-do apps and ended up feeling more behind

people with brain fog from long covid, a concussion, chronic illness, grief, new parenthood, menopause or depression, for whom holding a plan in their head has stopped working (named in the listing audience)
the person who has been avoiding a phone call for three weeks and saves phone-anxiety scripts and 'what to say' cards
the person with a bag or drawer of unopened mail (a doom pile) who searches paperwork organization and mail organization
people who save gentle, no-guilt systems: 'weekly reset for a bad week', 'planner that does not punish a missed day'

visualWorld.setting: A real home-admin corner seen from above or straight on: a desk or kitchen counter with the unopened mail pile, a phone that has to make a call, a laptop with the email that has not been sent, sticky notes, an index card holding the one next step, a wall calendar with one circled date. Flat, warm, slightly cluttered at the edges and calm in the middle, because every pin moves from many things to one thing. The product appears as itself: a phone showing one Companion question at a time, or one of the three real screens.

props.draw: Doom pile: 6 to 9 overlapping rectangles at -15 to +20 degrees. Kraft tan and off-white envelopes, each with a V flap (two lines meeting at the centre), some with a pale window rectangle, one with a small stamp square. A soft flat ellipse shadow under the pile. No legible words on the envelopes.
Paper shopping bag by a door: a trapezoid in kraft tan with two thin arc handles, 4 to 5 envelope tops poking out at angles. Door suggested by one tall rounded rectangle edge and a circle knob.
Three (or four) neat stacks of 3 to 4 envelopes each, edges offset by 4px so the stack reads, each sitting on a rounded-rect label tab in the accent soft colour. Labels are set in type, not drawn.

A round dial (circle, 2px ink stroke) with a small knob rectangle on top and a pie wedge filled in accent showing ten minutes of the face. One tick label '10' at most. Guide pins only: the product does not have a timer (time-blindness-planning guide says so).

A square with a slightly curled bottom-right corner (a darker triangle fold) and a 2-degree rotation. Butter yellow (the existing pop hsl(43 92% 70%)), blush, or accent soft. Text set in a handwriting font, 1 to 3 short lines.

A monitor (rounded rectangle on a short neck and oval foot) covered edge to edge with 9 sticky notes at random small rotations, overlapping each other and the screen bezel, each with one or two words from the real list.
A cream 5:3 rectangle with one accent rule across the top and four pale grey ruled lines. Holds exactly one step in handwriting. A small drop shadow so it lifts off the clutter behind it.

An index card with a small tab on the top edge, a tiny phone or envelope glyph in the corner, large curly quotation marks in accent, and the real opening line in serif. Can be paper-clipped (two nested rounded loops) to the phone or notepad.
Recipe-box style: a front panel trapezoid in accent strong, with 8 index cards fanned upward behind it, each with a staggered tab carrying one playbook title.

A spiral notepad: tall rectangle, a row of 10 small circles along the top for the spiral, pale horizontal rules, checkbox squares down the left with hand-drawn tick strokes (one quadratic curve each). Text in handwriting font.
Rounded board rectangle in kraft, a clip at the top (rounded rectangle with a circle cut-out), holding a notepad page.

Phone outline (rounded rectangle, notch pill), screen with a circle avatar, two concentric arcs radiating to suggest ringing out, and two round buttons at the bottom (accent and muted). No invented words on screen.

The existing device frame (creative/src/visual/Phone.tsx) holding either a real screen from creative/public/screens/ (alongside-workspace.png, alongside-help.png, alongside-life.png) or a drawn single Companion step card.

A drawn Companion step, clearly an illustration and not a fake screenshot: a rounded card on the product surface colour, the prompt in serif, a one-line 'why' in small grey sans, and choice pills (rounded rectangles, one filled with accent). Every string comes from the playbook file named on the pin.
The numerals 5 4 3 2 1 and 'Go' in accent, decreasing in size and opacity left to right, matching the product's real Call now countdown (ReadyStep.tsx, READY_COUNTDOWN_START = 5).

Phone on a nightstand: phone rectangle with a dark screen, one notification bubble (rounded rectangle, white at 90%) with two lines of real copy, a crescent moon glyph for quiet hours. The nightstand is a flat rectangle with a drawer line and knob.
Three rows, each a label in sans and a pill switch (rounded track, circle thumb); the first one on (accent track), the others off.

A laptop-style window: rounded rectangle with a title bar and three dots, two grey bars for To and Subject, the body with real text or just 'Hi,' and a vertical cursor bar in accent, and a Send pill bottom-left.
A month grid (7 by 5 squares) under a header band with two binder rings. One date circled with a hand-drawn loop in accent; optionally a sticky note attached to that square.
Circle face, 12 short ticks, two hands set to 3:30 (the guide's exact time), a centre dot in accent.

A two-page spread: left page with three days of dense scribble lines (abstract, not words), right page with one fully empty day box, ribbon bookmark hanging off the bottom. Envelopes from mail-pile overlapping one corner.
5 to 6 book spines of different heights and colours on a shelf line, each with a band or ribbon, one leaning; the point is several bought, none finished. No brand names.
Manila folder: rectangle with a tab on top, two sheets peeking out at an angle, a sticky note on the front.
The back of an envelope: rectangle with the four flap lines meeting at the centre, lying on the desk at a slight angle.
A trapezoid glass with a light blue fill to two thirds, a white highlight stroke, and a small ellipse for the rim.
An accent ribbon with a notched V tail, hanging off a card or page to mark the exact place.
Four shallow stacked letter trays (parallelograms with a front lip), each with a label tab carrying one of the four life shapes.
A flat top-down surface band in the product appBg with a subtle darker edge line; props cast short flat shadows (ellipses at 8% ink).
A closed laptop seen from above: rounded rectangle with a slightly darker hinge edge, a sticky note on the lid, a key ring (two circles and a key shape) beside it.
Hand-drawn editing marks in accent or ink: a strike-through line with a slight wobble, a circle loop, a tick. Used to cross out the 'not that' side and circle the 'this' side.
Cloud shape built from 5 overlapping circles, trailing two small circles toward the thinker point.
A flame shape and a progress ring arc with a percent glyph, each struck through with a marks strike. Used only to say the product has none of them.
Three to four soft overlapping circles at 30 to 40% opacity in the accent wash, drifting across the top of a scene.

visualWorld.palette: Ground: the product's own blush-grey (appBg #f4f0f1, wash #f7f1f3, paper #fcfafb), so pins stay light, which is what most top pins share. Ink #241e21 for type. Mulberry accent #86586a (strong #5f3d4b) only for the one thing: the circled date, the ticked box, the chosen card, the opening-line quote marks. Paper props carry the warmth: butter sticky notes (the existing pop hsl(43 92% 70%)), kraft envelope tan, cream index cards, a little blush. No new brand colours: the accent stays the only saturated colour, so a pin reads as this product even in a grid of other ADHD pins.
visualWorld.mood: Calm in the middle of the mess. Recognisable clutter at the edges (the pile, the wall of notes, the phone you are avoiding) and one clear, kind thing in the centre (one card, one line, one date). Never shaming, never 'productivity hack' loud, no red warning colours, no lateness marks on the product's own side.
visualWorld.type: Headline in Newsreader (already used), UI strings in IBM Plex Sans as the product uses them, and handwritten text on sticky notes, notepads and index cards. The creative engine has no handwriting font today (creative/public/fonts has Inter and Space Mono only), so one OFL handwriting face (for example Caveat or Patrick Hand from Google Fonts) needs adding before archetypes C, D and F can be rendered as described.

archetypes.name: The opening line card
archetypes.clicks: Phone-anxiety advice consistently says the opening is the hardest part and to write it word for word (EWU), and printable point-form script cards are a known save format in this exact niche (Life Skills Advocate's 'Before You Call' card). A pin that hands over the actual sentence is useful at a glance, which is what gets saved for later.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-330: headline in Newsreader, 64-76px, left-aligned with 72px side margins, max 3 lines. 360-1060: the script card, 820x520, rotated -2 degrees, centred, the real line in serif 42-48px inside large accent quote marks; behind its top-right corner, overlapping by 80px, the phone-outgoing-call or email-compose prop at 40% of card size. 1090-1240: sub line (one real line) in sans 30px, plus up to two small 'have in front of you' chips if the pin uses them. 1300-1440: product line (name and price, or 'Free guide'); small logo top-left, never bottom-right.
archetypes.visual: One index card with the real first sentence, paper-clipped to a ringing phone or stuck to an email window. For the eight-playbook pin, the card-file-box with eight tabbed cards.
archetypes.text: The opening line is copied verbatim from the playbook's suggestedWording (src/products/alongside/playbooks/*.ts) or, on guide pins, from the guide's scripts block in src/content/guides.ts. Situation labels come from the playbook's choices.
archetypes.bestFor: Phone calls you avoid, saying no, first line of an email, chasing a reply, the 'scripts for hard calls' Maple pin.

archetypes.name: Doom pile to piles
archetypes.clicks: 'Doom pile' (Didn't Organize, Only Moved) is established ADHD vocabulary (ADDitude, Psychology Today) and sort-into-categories methods like the doom diamond spread as practical how-tos (Apartment Therapy). A before-and-after transformation in one image shows the method working without reading, which suits a 1-second scroll.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-300: headline. 300-760: the mess, a wide mail-pile (or brain-dump scraps) drawn large and slightly cropped by the left and right edges so it feels too big. 760-840: a hand-drawn accent arrow or three short arrows fanning down. 840-1220: three or four neat stacks or trays side by side, each with a label tab in type, the 'act on this' stack ringed in accent. 1230-1290: sub line. 1310-1440: product line.
archetypes.visual: Unopened mail (or loose notes) becoming labelled stacks; for the product pin, the loose things drop into the four life-trays.
archetypes.text: Stack labels from the pin's own description or the linked guide; for the product, the four KIND_LABEL names in src/products/alongside/life.ts.
archetypes.bestFor: Paperwork and mail pins, the weekly reset (pull one thing out of the pile), 'what it holds' brain-dump pin.

archetypes.name: Sticky notes on the thing
archetypes.clicks: Visible sticky notes are the most common ADHD advice for keeping a task in sight (Focus Bear, URMC: 'get options out of your head and onto paper or sticky notes'), and Pinterest's 2026 forecast reports renewed interest in handwriting. A handwritten note stuck on a real object is instantly recognisable as 'my desk' to this audience.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-280: headline. 280-1100: one object drawn large (monitor, laptop lid, phone, folder, mail pile) with sticky notes on it. Variant 'too many': 6-9 notes covering the object, with one index card held in front at 1.15 scale, centred at y 860. Variant 'one note': a single sticky note at 1.6 scale, centred, its words readable at thumbnail size (min 44px handwriting). 1120-1260: sub line. 1300-1440: product line.
archetypes.visual: The real list on notes (from the guide), or the one real next step on one note, stuck where you will pass it.
archetypes.text: Note contents are copied from guide examples (first-physical-step, task paralysis, to-do lists, restart, planners, time blindness) or from the pin's own Maple points.
archetypes.bestFor: To-do lists, task paralysis, leave yourself a note, 'later today is not a time', planners.

archetypes.name: The notepad checklist
archetypes.clicks: Checklists and how-tos are the formats Pinterest business users most often report earning saves and clicks (Pinterest Business Community), and they are the save-for-later format by nature: the pin is the tool. Brain-dump worksheets are a whole printable category in this niche (Etsy, Gumroad, Payhip).
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-300: headline. 300-1180: a notepad or clipboard, 760px wide, rotated 1.5 degrees, with 3 to 4 items in handwriting 38-44px, each with a checkbox; ticks drawn in accent; a prop at the pad's lower edge (glass of water, folder, small phone) overlapping by 60px to say where this happens. 1200-1270: sub line. 1300-1440: product line. Keep to 4 items: more becomes unreadable on mobile.
archetypes.visual: A spiral notepad page with real items, three or four, some ticked.
archetypes.text: Items verbatim from a playbook's prepare/check items or step prompts, or from the guide list the pin links to. Never more items than the source has.
archetypes.bestFor: What to have ready, the three checks before sending, three questions, a system for bill dates, the Maple '3 ways' list.

archetypes.name: One question on the phone
archetypes.clicks: Shop-link pins need to show what the thing is. A real or faithfully drawn app screen tells the viewer this is a tool, not another $2 printable (brain-dump printables sell for a few dollars on Etsy, which is the comparison the listing wants to avoid). One question per screen also proves the product's promise in the picture itself.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-300: headline. 300-1180: phone-frame, 470px wide, centred or offset right to x 560 with one supporting prop on the left (bookmark ribbon, calendar, clock, fog). Inside: either a real screen from creative/public/screens/ (crop out the Next.js dev 'N' badge at bottom-left, it is in all three captures) or a drawn step-card with real strings. 1200-1270: sub line. 1300-1440: product line with the real price from the listing.
archetypes.visual: One Companion step on a phone: the question, the why line, and the choices, one of them in accent.
archetypes.text: Prompts, whys, choices and placeholders from the playbook files; outcome labels from OUTCOME_OPTIONS in src/components/product-shell/companion/steps.ts; ready-step strings from src/components/product-shell/companion/ReadyStep.tsx; quiet line from src/products/alongside/attention.ts.
archetypes.bestFor: Pins that link to /shop/alongside and describe a specific behaviour of the app.

archetypes.name: The relatable scene
archetypes.clicks: Relatable 'POV' and 'tell me without telling me' framing is how this niche talks about itself, and the Maple account already uses it. A wordless scene of the face-down letter, the planner under the post, or the draft rewritten four times gets the 'that's me' recognition that drives saves, with the headline doing the talking.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-360: headline, larger than other archetypes (76-88px) because the scene carries no text; for Maple POV pins, inside a speech bubble. 360-1180: a full-width scene, top-down or straight-on, with 4 to 6 props and one small accent detail that resolves it (an index card, a bookmark, a notification). 1200-1270: sub line. 1300-1440: product line.
archetypes.visual: A specific domestic moment from the guide's own 'say it's...' example, drawn wordlessly.
archetypes.text: Only the headline, the sub, and at most one short real string inside the scene.
archetypes.bestFor: Guide pins that open with a scenario, Maple POV pins, the missed-week and planner pins, lock-screen reminder pin.

archetypes.name: Two columns: this, not that
archetypes.clicks: Side-by-side 'instead of / try' comparisons let a viewer get the whole idea in one look and are a common shape for ADHD tips. Measured data on comparison pins is thin (see the brief), but the guides already contain real two-column material, so the format costs nothing to try and contrasts well with the other archetypes in a feed.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-280: headline. 300-340: two column labels in sans caps, left muted, right accent. 360-1180: two columns 410px wide with a 40px gutter; left items struck through with marks, right items circled or ticked; one small prop at the head of each column (sticky note vs clock, page stack vs bookmark). 1200-1270: sub line. 1300-1440: product line.
archetypes.visual: Crossed-out vague version on the left, the concrete version on the right.
archetypes.text: Both columns copied from a guide table or compare block (time-blindness 'Vague versus exact', weekly reset 'Two kinds of reset', first-physical-step tables) or from the ready step's two real buttons.
archetypes.bestFor: Time blindness, first physical step, weekly reset, call now or name a time, planners that grade you.

notes: Product line: name and price come from src/shop/products/alongside.ts at render time (currently $49, compare at $99), never typed on the pin.

All three real screens (creative/public/screens/alongside-*.png) show the Next.js dev indicator ('N' circle, bottom-left); crop or mask it before use. Their items (dental check, insurance, car hire) are demo data in a real UI, which is fine to show as UI but should not be quoted as claims.
The kitchen-timer prop is only for guide pins: the time-blindness guide states the Companion does not do timers. The only timed thing in the product is the 5-second Call now countdown.
Keep logos small and out of the bottom-right corner, where Pinterest overlays its own icons.
